welcome.autosave:
There's now a folder named Twine in your Documents folder. Inside that is a Stories folder, where all your work will be saved. Twine saves as you work, so you don't have to worry about remembering to save it yourself. You can always open the folder your stories are saved to by using the Show Library item in the Twine menu.

Because Twine is always saving your work, the files in your story library will be locked from editing while Twine is open.

If you'd like to open a Twine story file you received from someone else, you can import it into your library using the Import From File link in the story list.
welcome.browserStorage:
That means you don't need to create an account to use Twine 2, and everything you create isn't stored on a server somewhere else—it stays right in your browser.

Two very important things to remember, though. Since your work is saved only in your browser, if you clear its saved data, then you'll lose your work! Not good. Remember to use that Archive button often. You can also publish individual stories to files using the menu on each story in the story list. Both archive and story files can always be re-imported into Twine.

Secondly, anyone who can use this browser can see and make changes to your work. So if you've got a nosy kid brother, look into setting up a separate profile for yourself.
welcome.browserStorageTitle: Your work is only saved in your browser
welcome.done: Thanks for reading, and have fun with Twine.
welcome.greeting: Twine is an open-source tool for telling interactive, nonlinear stories. There are a few things you should know before you get started.
welcome.help: If you've never used Twine before, then welcome! The Twine Cookbook is a great resource for learning how to use it. If you haven't used Twine before, it's a great place to start.

problems.badVar: Progress variable name: Latin letters, no spaces.

codes.askPinCondition: The terminal will ask for a personal code: this code is used in an “employee entered a code” condition.
codes.decoderHint: For tidiness only: the list filter uses this mark. The code can be entered in any field that checks the shared table. Whether it is too early is decided by “When it can be entered” or by the “Access” of the screen it leads to.
codes.decoderDigits: This code has more than digits: it cannot be typed into a “Digits only” field.
codes.whenHint: Too early, the code is not used up and its actions and answer do not run. For a code leading to a closed screen, that screen's “Access” is enough.
codes.phoneOnlyNote: A phone app code (the terminal ignores it). The phone answer and actions are below; the label is the code comment in the package.
codes.phoneBothNote: The code works on the terminal and on phones: each has its own answer and actions — tabs «On the terminal» and «On the phone».

events.title: Event
events.when: When the terminal goes to this screen
events.repeat: Repeat — when the condition becomes true again
events.repeatHint: Unchecked — once per game. Checked — every time the condition goes from false to true.
events.delay: Seconds after the condition became true
events.delayHint: 0 — at once. The countdown runs in the background and survives screen changes and crashes; if the condition turns false meanwhile, it is cancelled.
events.priorityHint: If several events are ready at once, the higher number goes first (default 0). The next one waits until players leave the event screen.
events.hint: The terminal goes to this screen by itself when the condition becomes true. An open message window closes. To bring players back, add a link with the action “Return to the previous screen”. In the text: first line <<sg-event …>> and tag sg-event.
events.confirmRemove: The screen stops being an event (the first line <<sg-event …>> and the tag are removed, the rest of the text stays). Remove?
events.noTag: The passage has no sg-event tag — the terminal will not go to it.
events.stay: Don't go to the screen — actions only
events.stayHint: The terminal stays on its screen; the event only runs the actions below. This passage's text is not shown to players.
events.doHint: Run once when the event fires (before going to the screen). In text — <<sg-event-do>>…<</sg-event-do>>, invisible on screen.
events.hintStay: The terminal runs the actions when the condition becomes true and stays on its screen. First line <<sg-event stay …>> and tag sg-event. All events and phone rules — Events window (Story tab).
events.whenStay: When the event fires (the terminal stays on its screen)
events.popup: Don't go to the screen — show a message window
events.popupHint: The terminal stays on its screen and the text of this passage appears on top as a message window (with its own title or the passage name). If another window is open, the event waits until it is closed. The actions below run too.
events.whenPopup: When the event fires (a message window over the screen)
events.hintPopup: The terminal shows a message window with this passage's text when the condition becomes true and stays on its screen. In the text: first line <<sg-event popup …>> and the sg-event tag.
events.ackHint: No close cross; a click outside does not close it — players will read it.

ticker.title: Event line

intro.news: Messages of the top line on the main screen. Conditions and limits are checked all the time on any screen; the line is shown on the main screen only.
intro.line: The line sits on one screen only. Its frame matches the terminal window. On-screen buttons from the top corners move down by the line height.
intro.cycle: “Цикл XXXXX” in the top right corner. Its value depends on the progress variable.

ticker.demoHint: Main screen preview: settings apply at once, no sound.

news.name: Name
news.nameHint: For you only, players do not see it. Each message has its own name.
news.textHint: You can insert a variable: <<= $name>>. Text that fits stays still, longer text scrolls.
news.generalHint: Only one general message is shown: the one switched on last. Otherwise it takes turns with the others.
news.minutesHint: 0 — no limit. Counted on any screen.
news.priorityHint: Within the queue: higher goes first. Equal — by list order.

line.screenHint: The screen that shows the line. By default — the story's start screen.
line.speedHint: For text that does not fit in the line.
line.pauseHint: How long the text stays before it moves.
line.holdHint: For text that fits. Long text changes once it has scrolled.
line.orderHint: Message queue. Within each group — by priority, then list order.

cycle.variableHint: When the variable changes, the cycle changes.
cycle.rowsHint: The row with the highest progress not above the current one is used. None — 00000.
cycle.spinTitle: Digit change on the main screen
cycle.spinHint: Only changed digits and those to the right of them spin. The rightmost stops first.
cycle.soundHint: Plays when players see the counter: on entering the main screen, or at once if they are already there.
cycle.gapHint: Time until the next digit to the left stops. 0 means all at once.
cycle.ratesHint: Changes per second. Speed moves smoothly from start to end and cuts off when the digit stops. Gradual slowdown: 20 and 2. Almost no slowdown and a sharp stop: 30 and 20.
cycle.fontHint: Default is DSEG7, as on the timer display.

screens.none: No screen views yet: create them in Terminal Appearance
screens.intro: A preset for special screens: lockdown, alarm, loading. Assign it with the Screen view button above the text. Anything not set comes from the General tab. The preview on the right shows the chosen view on the chosen screen; nothing is written to the story.
screens.name: Name
screens.nameHint: You can rename it: screens keep the view.

list.confirmDeleteUsed: Screen view “{{name}}” is used by {{count}} screen(s). They will become regular. Delete?

screens.sizeHint: On-screen buttons and pictures stay where they are on regular screens.
screens.winBgHint: For a full fill: full-screen window and a custom window background.
screens.textColorHint: Link and button colors come from their kind.

textStyles.none: No text styles yet: create them in Terminal Appearance
textStyles.intro: A preset for individual text: select it in the passage and pick a style with the Text style button. Anything not set stays as the surrounding text. The preview shows a sample; it is not written to the story.
textStyles.name: Name
textStyles.lineHeightHint: Text with its own spacing becomes a separate block: good for a paragraph, not a word within a line.

list.confirmDeleteUsed: Style “{{name}}” is used on {{count}} screen(s). The text stays, without the style. Delete?

access.title: Screen access
access.sharedHint: One for the whole game, for screens without their own. It is an ordinary passage and gets the sg-lock tag.
access.noLock: No lock passage is chosen. Until one is, a link with this behavior cannot be clicked and a code answers “Wrong code”.
access.sourcesHint: What each source does while the screen is closed. The top row of a group is the default; below it each source can have its own behavior.
access.hint: The condition is checked all the time: a link appears as soon as the screen opens. A code is checked before its actions, so an early code is not used up. The preview shows all links; check with Play. In the text: the first line <<sg-access …>> and the sg-access tag.
access.confirmRemove: The screen becomes open to everyone (the <<sg-access …>> command and the tag are removed, the rest of the text stays). Remove?
access.noTag: The passage has no sg-access tag: the terminal lets everyone through.

articles.title: Article
articles.name: Title in the list
articles.sectionHint: No commas. The section joins the choice list once the text is saved.
articles.orderHint: Lower number goes higher; ties go by title. Sections follow their topmost article.
articles.backHint: Empty: the shared caption from Terminal appearance → Articles.
articles.hint: The article appears in “Article list” blocks by itself. The terminal adds a “Back” link at the bottom, leading to the screen the article was opened from. To close an article use “Access”, like any screen.
articles.noTag: This passage has no sg-article tag, so lists will not show it.
articles.confirmRemove: The passage stops being an article and leaves the lists. The text stays. Remove?

first.none: No ways yet — create them in “Terminal appearance”
first.intro: How the elements of a screen appear when players enter it for the first time. A way is set only on the screens you choose: use the “First visit” button above the screen text. Later visits and a restore after a crash open the screen as usual. The “Show” button above the preview plays the selected way on the selected screen.
first.name: Name
first.timeHint: Noise or interference fades to zero over this time.
first.stepHint: Elements go from top to bottom; a line of text is one element. 0 — all together.
first.color: Colour of noise and interference lines
first.skip: A click shows everything at once
first.skipHint: Links and buttons that have not appeared yet cannot be clicked.
first.howTo: Glitch colours are the ones in “Text effects” on the “General” tab. The alarm screen is not affected.

list.confirmDeleteUsed: Way “{{name}}” is used on {{count}} screen(s). They will open as usual. Delete?

first.soundHint: Plays once per screen, from the first element to the end of the file. A click or leaving the screen does not cut it off.

tips.title: Hover tooltip
tips.contentHint: The cursor rests on it. It can hold a link.
tips.widthHint: 0 means as in Terminal appearance. Short text takes only the room it needs.

check.title: Story check
check.intro: Things that will show up as errors in the live game. The story is not changed; click a passage name to open it.
check.noFolder: No game folder chosen — files were not checked.

kinds.media: File missing from the game folder

hints.media: The path is written in the story, but the file is not in the game folder.

hints.code: The code has no actions, no answer and no destination.

hints.app: App data in the story (App window, blocks, phone characters and codes) — like the app editor "Check" tab: ✗ — error, ⚠ — worth checking.

copies.title: Radio tracks without a reversed copy
copies.hint: The story has a radio with reverse: these tracks can't play backwards yet (the game shows “REVERSE UNAVAILABLE”). Copies are also made when you press Save in the Music and Radio windows.

music.title: Music
music.intro: The shared player catalogue: Atmosphere and Radio sections with folders and tracks. One track plays at a time; one volume (00–99).
music.spinHint: Digits spin and stop right to left. 0 — at once.
music.autoHint: When a track ends, the next one of the folder plays.
music.tracksHint: Track order is the AUTO order.
music.when: When the track is in the catalogue
music.startHint: On first play the shared volume becomes this.

problems.emptyTrack: A track has no name or file.
problems.slash: A track name contains “/”: that is how “Folder/Track” is written.
problems.noTarget: A transmission leads to a radio folder that does not exist.

music.tipHint: Shown on hover in the Atmosphere catalog.
music.airHint: Transmissions for the repaired radio: each time the screen opens they take random places on the dial. A caught transmission appears in its radio folder.
music.confirmDeleteNested: Delete folder “{{name}}” with its subfolders ({{nested}}) and all tracks?
music.gainHint: 100% — as recorded. Make a loud file quieter to match others; the overall 00–99 volume applies on top.
music.toHint: The caught transmission appears in this radio folder.
music.toNone: Nowhere: interference, never in the catalog
music.widthHint: How many MHz on each side of the transmission it is heard. Closer needle — louder.
music.textHint: Shown in the radio ticker until caught. Empty — the radio view message.
music.whenAir: When the transmission is on air
music.reverseHint: What is heard while REVERSE is held. Empty — the program reverses the track on Save.
music.jamHint: Interference of radios with the air: one folder per radio view from the Radio window, in its order (folders are not created by hand). Each time the radio screen opens, “from”…“to” pieces land on the dial: one already caught piece of this radio, the rest not yet caught ones of this radio and the radios above it; if short — more caught ones of this radio. Interference can be caught like a transmission: it goes to the radio catalog, folder “Interference”.
music.jamMigrated: Interference of radio “{{names}}” moved here from the Radio window. Press Save.
music.jamFolderHint: Named after the radio view: rename the view in the Radio window, the folder follows.
music.jamOrphan: There is no radio view with this name. This interference is not used — the folder can be deleted.
music.whenJam: When this interference can land on the dial
music.jamWidthHint: How many MHz on each side of its spot it can be heard.

screenMusic.title: Screen music
screenMusic.intro: Change music some seconds after entering.
screenMusic.afterHint: From the start of the fade.

radio.title: Radio
radio.name: Look name
radio.nameHint: Radio blocks find the look by name.
radio.typeHint: Repaired — with the air; with reverse — plus REVERSE and reels; with decoder — as with reverse plus DECODE and a picture window. Progress bar and SHUFFLE — on all.
radio.elementsHint: Everything without its own colour below.
radio.label: Frame label
radio.confirmDeleteUsed: Look “{{name}}” is used on {{count}} screens. Delete?

problems.slash: A view name can't contain “/” (it names the interference folder in the Music window).

radio.airHint: Scale 88–108 MHz, drag the needle, −/+ move 0.1 at most once a second. Landing on a broadcast with the buttons lights the lamp. SEARCH pauses catalogue music. Broadcasts are in the Music window, Air section.
radio.incomingHint: The ticker shows it while an uncaught transmission is on air. A transmission may have its own.
radio.catchHint: Seconds the needle must stay exactly on a transmission to catch it.
radio.noiseHint: Plays in its ranges, quieter near transmissions and interference, silent on exact tuning.
radio.jamsHint: Each time the screen opens a random set is chosen and placed randomly on the dial; nearby ones play together.
radio.jamWidthHint: How many MHz on each side it is heard.
radio.jamsMaxHint: In this radio's folder: {{files}}; not yet caught interference of the radios above also lands. Each piece — once.
radio.asFrame: Now the same as the frame: partitions, grille, reels.
radio.reverseHint: While REVERSE is held the track plays backwards. The program makes reversed copies on Save (here and in Music), into media/audio/reverse.
radio.decoderHint: DECODE turns the decoder on: if the playing track or the loudest spot of the air carries an SSTV picture, it builds line by line in time with the sound; off-tune — noisy lines, not SSTV — garbage lines. Click the window — full terminal, click again — back. Pictures are taken from interference and transmissions when you press Save in the Music window.
radio.jamsMoved: Interference of this radio is in the Music window, section Interference, folder “{{name}}” (now: {{count}}). Here — how many land at once.
radio.orderHint: The order of views is the order of radios in the game: interference of the radios above also lands on the radios below.

reverse.noFolder: No game folder — reversed copies not made.

sstv.working: Looking for SSTV pictures in interference and transmissions: {{done}} of {{total}}…
sstv.noFolder: No game folder — SSTV pictures were not searched.

app.title: Players' phone app
app.intro: The players' app content lives in this story: the «Приложение» passage (settings, chapters, devices, notices, alarms, glitches, rules, votes), data blocks — passages tagged app-block (folders in the name: «Folder/Block»), characters and phone codes — in «Коды» (a character is the employee with the same number). Images and sounds — in the game folder media/app/.
app.empty: No app data in this story. Load a package from the app editor.
app.noFolder: No game folder chosen: app images and sounds are kept in it (media/app/). Choose it in the story details.
app.diffTitle: What will change in the story
app.firstLoad: The story has no app data yet — everything from the package will be added.
app.numbered: Characters without a terminal number got numbers: {{list}}.
app.filesSkipped: No game folder — package files ({{n}}) were not saved.
app.publishHint: Checks the story first, then builds the package into the game folder.
app.publishPhone: {{passage}}: "To phones: …" — {{detail}} is not in the app
app.publishOk: Story check: no errors or warnings.
app.publishErrors: Story check before publishing: {{n}} errors. The package was not built.
app.publishForced: Built although the check found errors ({{n}}).

phone.noAccounts: No app characters yet: in «Коды» → Employees, tick «App character on the phone».
phone.noBlocks: No app blocks yet: a passage with the «App block» button above the text.
phone.confirmTerminalOnly: The code will be terminal-only: its phone part (phone answer and actions) will be removed. Continue?
phone.badPhone: Phone data can't be read (broken JSON) — fix the «Коды» passage text or load the package again.
phone.labelPhoneHint: For yourself: what the code is for, where it lies. In the package it is the code comment (editor and code table only).
phone.whereHint: The terminal and phones check codes separately. A «both» code has its own answer and actions on the terminal and on the phone.
phone.whereBoth: on the terminal and on phones

problems.sameLogin: Same login codes for app characters: {{list}}.

voiceWhy.unknown: «{{word}}»: the model doesn't know this word — use a synonym or another form (check again on the phone).
voiceWhy.latin: «{{word}}»: Latin letters — the model is Russian, write it in Russian as it sounds.
voiceWhy.digits: «{{word}}»: digits in a phrase — write them as words; bare digits are recognised without a phrase.
voiceWhy.abbr: «{{word}}»: looks like an abbreviation — write it as spoken or use a word.

act.unknown: Action «{{type}}» — edit it in the app editor.
act.fixHint: A repair code is usually entered on the glitching phone («whoever entered the code»). «Selected» and «everyone» remove it on other phones via the network.
act.appHint: The device appears only if the character is ticked in the device's «Available to».
act.eventHint: The terminal (condition «Came from a phone → event») and rules (Network & events → Rules) receive it.

color.any-on: allow changing any time (until chapter end)
color.any-off: forbid changing any time (until chapter end)

act.termSharedHint: Shared variable: the center sets it for everyone.
act.torchHint: Phone torch (in the preview — a screen flash). While the app is open.

block.noTag: The passage has no app-block tag — without it the block won't get into the package.
block.name: Folder: {{folder}}; title: {{title}}.

block.textHint: The passage text after the first line is the block text (app markup: *bold*, # headings).
block.id: Block id in the package: {{id}} (the package recognises the block by it).
block.whoHint: Others won't see this block even with the code.
block.startHint: Otherwise a code opens it (action «Open blocks» or «Opens blocks» of a phone code).

block.garbleHint: Until this chapter the player sees garbled characters; from it — the real text.

block.noFolder: The game folder is not chosen: block files live in its media/app/ (story Details).
block.caption: Caption
block.mediaHint: The image or sound line goes where the cursor is in the passage text (at the start of a line — before it, otherwise after it). Put new files into the game folder media/app/.
block.confirmRemove: Remove the block's first line and the app-block tag? The passage text stays.
block.hidden: Hidden: opened only by a code, not shown in the list

code.appHint: Only with this device's camera, no typing.
code.noteHint: Players don't see it; printed under the QR.
code.chapterHint: Earlier the app answers «code not active yet».
code.comment: Phone comment (what the code is for)
code.voiceHint: Words as spoken (case, punctuation and ё don't matter). Works for characters with the Voice function who can use the code. Empty code — voice only.
code.voiceMaxHint: 0 — all who heard it. 1 — one: the phone asks the centre first, the first one wins.
code.voiceEveryHint: 0 — no pause. E.g. 60 — at most once a minute (for everyone, via the centre).
code.term: For the terminal: any phone with voice hears it and silently passes it to the terminal
code.termHint: П-60: nothing happens on the phone; the centre tells the terminal it was heard (condition «Came from a phone → code or phrase»). One phone passes it by default.
code.opensTitle: Who it opens for and what it shows
code.answer: Answer (text in the window after entry)
code.answers: Next times — other answers (the last one repeats)
code.perAcc: Only once per character («you already got it»)
code.emptyText: When everything is taken (empty — common text)
code.mineText: When this character already took (empty — common text)
code.netHint: Such a code asks the network centre. Without a connection the phone answers «no connection».
code.noNetHint: A code without limits works without the network too.
code.variantsHint: E.g. a stimulant: one text for the Medic, another for the Engineer. The most precise variant wins.
code.othersNone: The code is open to all characters. Tick above who it opens for to set an answer for others here.
code.deniedAsWrong: For others — like a wrong code (nothing happens)
code.actionsHint: Run when the code works on the phone. «Everyone» and «selected» go through the network.

code.whenNoShared: No shared variables: Variables window → «Shared with phones».
code.whenValueHint: A number as a number, yes/no, anything else as text (only «equals» and «not equal»).

code.whenMode: If the condition is not met
code.whenModeInactive: “CODE NOT ACTIVE YET” and the answer

person.title: On the phone

person.confirmOff: Remove the app character (name, login, functions, colours) from this employee?
person.name: Name (in the app header)
person.loginHint: The game master enters it on the player's phone at the start.
person.modulesHint: Ticked — on from the chosen chapter. Unticked or earlier — as chosen on the right. A code («App function» action) can turn it on, off or break it.

person.notesHint: Shown in the character’s NOTES tab (needs the Notes function).

general.title: Title (shown on the login screen)
general.versionHint: Grows by itself on each «Build package».
general.masterCodeHint: Opens the master mode on any phone. Better 8–16 digits.

votes.chapters: Repeat only in chapters (nothing ticked — all)
votes.termHint: The terminal gets the vote result.

voice.intro: Offline speech recognition on the phone (Vosk, small Russian model). The phone knows only code phrases and digits. A phrase is a code: who, chapter, answer and actions — in the «Коды» window.
voice.minConfHint: Lower — works with unclear speech, but more often «hears» it in conversation.
voice.sensHint: The recogniser runs only when the volume is above noise. Saves battery.
voice.digits: Digits by voice — like a typed code (in the background — existing codes only)
voice.whoHint: Characters are «Коды» employees with phone data. Turn voice on during the game with a code.
voice.phrasesHint: The rest (who, answer, actions) — «Коды» → code → On the phone. A longer phrase wins over a shorter one.
voice.unknownHint: Copy the «Model doesn't know» line from the phone's «Voice: check» window here — phrases get hints.
voice.batteryText:
1. Charge the phone to 100 %.
2. Master mode → «Voice: check and measure» → «Start».
3. 2 hours in each mode.
4. The measure window shows «% per hour»; the difference from «off» is the cost of voice.

preview.title: Phone preview
preview.hint: This is how the app looks on a phone: codes and blocks work, no network, nothing is saved. Unsaved changes are shown too.
preview.missing: Files missing in the game folder: {{list}}

blocks.title: Blocks by folder
blocks.hint: A block folder comes from the passage name ("Plans/Bay 1/Map") or the folder word. Left: folders (in brackets — blocks with subfolders) and blocks; click a block to open its passage. Renaming and new blocks go into the story at once.
blocks.renameHint: Subfolders with "/"; all blocks of the folder and its subfolders are renamed. Empty — blocks leave the folder.
blocks.newTitleHint: May include a subfolder: "Bay 2/Map" — the block goes into a new folder inside the selected one.
blocks.added: Passage "{{name}}" created (tag app-block). Open it to write the text.

qr.title: Code to QR
qr.hint: The QR holds the code itself — the same one typed by hand. Put the JPG on a terminal screen (players scan it) or print it for props.
qr.caption: Caption
qr.colorsHint: The Signaly app reads green on black; ordinary scanners sometimes do not. For print, black on white or black on green is safer.
qr.empty: Type a code — the QR appears here.

sstv.title: SSTV: image → sound
sstv.hint: Sound for the terminal (decoder radio or a plain track), a speaker or props. Phones do not receive SSTV (P-45).
sstv.file: Image (media/app/ and media/img/ of the game folder)
sstv.label: Label before the image (code, optional)
sstv.labelHint: A short sound code before the transmission (app format).
sstv.decoded: How the terminal decoder draws it (clean sound):
sstv.toTerminal: To the game folder (media/audio/sstv/) — for Music
sstv.toApp: To media/app/ — sound for an app block
sstv.savedTerminal: Saved: {{path}}. Add it as a track in the Music window.
sstv.savedApp: Saved: {{path}}. Use it in a block (App block → + Sound).
sstv.codeHint: A short beep (1–3 s) carrying the code — a "data transmission" for the terminal or props.

header.title: First line
header.titleHint: Empty — the character name. {name}, {prof}, {chapter}, {{v}} — a shared variable.
header.chapter: Show the chapter on the right
header.itemsHint: A line under the name: a shared variable as a number («7» or «7/10») or as lit and unlit squares. The label may be empty.
header.noShared: No shared variables: Variables window → «Shared with phones».
header.label: Label
header.cellsHint: As many lit as the value; 0 — by value (up to 10). Yes/no — one square.
header.infoHint: Tapping the header opens a window with all indicators and the sections below.
header.menuHint: Order (↑), own names and hidden tabs.
header.chaptersHint: From chapter N — own lines and summary title (an empty field — as in the common header). Lasts until the next such entry.
header.asCommon: Empty — as in the common header.
header.fitHint: Divisions shrink or stretch: a scale of 10 and of 100 have the same length.
header.overHint: Above the maximum — as many divisions glitch as the excess (scale 10: 12 — the first 2).
header.lowHint: Empty — no alarm. Below the threshold — alarm color, blinking.
header.limitsHint: The network center keeps the value within the limit (terminal, codes, console, rules): “+1” at the maximum keeps the maximum. What to do at that moment — the “Events” window → phone condition “hit the limit”. Empty — no limit.
header.layersHint: Layer 1 — values 1…N, layer 2 — N+1…2N, etc.: the scale fills again with its own effect. The variable cannot go above N × layers; on the last layer the scale stays full. Empty — no layers (then «Overload» works).
header.tapsHint: The header has several tap places: name, chapter (right), each indicator (set at the indicator). «By place»: name — character dossier, chapter — chapter window, indicator — its details.
header.about: Window when the chapter is tapped
header.aboutHint: Empty — as in the previous entry; none — common summary.

eventsWindow.title: Events
eventsWindow.intro: When X → do Y. A terminal condition is run by the terminal (goes to the event screen or only runs actions, including "To phones: …"). A phone condition (event, chapter + N minutes, every N minutes, shared variable) is run by the network center on the master's phone. Nothing is written until Save.
eventsWindow.termGroupHint: ▶ — goes to the screen, 💬 — a message window over the screen, ⚡ — actions only. Passages tagged sg-event.
eventsWindow.whoCenter: Runs on: the network center (master's phone), even when the terminal is busy or offline.
eventsWindow.removed: No longer an event. Save — the passage stays a plain screen.
eventsWindow.whoPhone: Runs: the phone itself (Android service — also in the background).
